title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS SWACHH SURVEKSHAN AWARDS
subtitle: CLEANLINESS IS NOT MERELY A MATTER OF MAINTAINING THE AESTHETIC APPEAL OF PUBLIC SPACES; IT IS ALSO AN INDICATOR OF OUR HEALTH, SOCIAL CONSCIOUSNESS, AND ADMINISTRATIVE ACCOUNTABILITY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 8:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 in New Delhi today (November 11, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that a single organization alone cannot achieve the goals of cleanliness. It requires the participation of every citizen, every household, every community, and every city. She underlined that cleanliness is not merely a matter of maintaining the aesthetic appeal of public spaces. It is also an indicator of our health, social consciousness, and administrative accountability. It is a reflection of our habits at home too.
The President said that every citizen, especially youth, women, Resident Welfare Associations and community organizations, should engage with various aspects of cleanliness. They should share their experiences and report any shortcomings, the resolution of which could help make our cities cleaner and healthier. This should foster an ongoing dialogue between the municipal administration and the citizens, thereby strengthening trust, transparency, and accountability.
The President said that citizens are the best judges when it comes to assessing the cleanliness of their surroundings. Therefore, the use of citizen feedback should not be limited merely to surveys or rankings. Instead, this feedback should serve as a vital tool for improving municipal services and addressing local challenges.
The President said that there is a need to develop effective, affordable and safe technologies in the field of sanitation. She was happy to note that various institutions, including several IITs and other scientific research organizations, are actively working in this direction.
The President noted that several startups have emerged in the sanitation sector. She said that such enterprises can contribute significantly toward solving real-world sanitation challenges while also creating employment opportunities.
The President said that there is a need to place special emphasis on enhancing the capacities of Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, as these are the fastest-growing urban centers. They have distinct needs and challenges. Their development should take place within a national framework designed to address their specific problems and challenges. She said planners in Tier-2 cities can learn from the issues faced by Tier-1 cities, and to do so, they should study the experiences of planners in Tier-1 cities.
The Swachh Survekshan Awards, organized by the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, honours India’s cleanest cities and recognizes their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban.

title: Vice President graces the 105th Foundation Day celebrations of Tamilnad Mercantile Bank (TMB) in Thoothukudi
subtitle:
TMB’s 105-year journey is a testament to its commitment to trust, service and financial inclusion

Banks must support MSMEs, farmers, entrepreneurs and women-led enterprises to realise Viksit Bharat @2047
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today graced the 105th Foundation Day celebrations of Tamilnad Mercantile Bank (TMB) in Thoothukudi, and called upon the bank to aspire to become one of India’s leading private sector banks in the coming years.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 105th Foundation Day celebrations of Tamilnad Mercantile Bank in Thoothukudi today.

Congratulating the bank on its remarkable 105-year journey, he highlighted its contribution to India’s economic growth and called upon banks to strengthen financial inclusion, support entrepreneurs, MSMEs, farmers and women-led enterprises, and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, TMB Part Time Chairman Shri K. Ramachandran, MD & CEO Shri Salee S. Nair, Executive Director Shri Vincent Menachery, members of the Board and senior officials were present on the occasion.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 11, 2026
Congratulating the bank on its remarkable 105-year journey, the Vice President recalled its origins in 1921 as Nadar Bank Limited and commended its contribution to the country’s banking sector.He said that, from its humble beginnings, the bank has grown into a major banking institution with 632 branches across 17 States and four Union Territories, serving over 53 lakh customers and recording total business exceeding ₹1.30 lakh crore.
Highlighting the vital role of banks in nation-building, he emphasised the importance of responsible lending and extending financial support to MSMEs, farmers, small traders, entrepreneurs, women-led enterprises and corporates.
The Vice President noted India’s remarkable economic progress and said that the banking sector has a crucial role in realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. He highlighted the transformation brought about by digital banking and UPI, as well as the expansion of financial inclusion, which has enabled more people to access formal banking services.
Commending TMB’s recent performance and technological progress, he urged the bank to continue strengthening cybersecurity, safeguarding customers’ money and personal data, and embracing innovation. He also stressed that the bank should remain rooted in Thoothukudi, its place of origin, even as it expands its national presence.
The Vice President expressed confidence that Tamilnad Mercantile Bank would continue to scale greater heights and establish itself among India’s leading private sector banks.
Tamil Nadu Governor Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, TMB Part Time Chairman Shri K. Ramachandran, Managing Director and CEO Shri Salee S. Nair, Executive Director Shri
Vincent Menachery, members of the Board and senior officials were present on the occasion.

title: BUILDING A STRONGER AND MORE PROSPEROUS INDIA REQUIRES EFFECTIVE INSTITUTIONS AND PUBLIC SERVANTS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
subtitle:
TECHNOLOGY MUST BE LEVERAGED TO PREVENT AND DETECT CRIME AND STRENGTHEN INTERNAL SECURITY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER INTERACTS WITH IPS PROBATIONERS IN PARLIAMENT HOUSE COMPLEX
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that building a stronger and more prosperous India requires effective institutions and public servants who are responsive to the aspirations and concerns of citizens. He underlined that police officers must maintain constant engagement with the public, communicate with people regularly, and develop a close understanding of their needs and challenges. He said that public trust is the cornerstone of effective policing. He called upon the probationers to earn the confidence of citizens through impartiality, transparency, accessibility and prompt action. He observed that the police must be perceived not merely as an agency responsible for maintaining law and order, but also as a dependable institution that stands with people and safeguards their rights and security.
Shri Birla made these remarks while interacting with a group of IPS probationers at the Parliament House Complex. He called upon them to dedicate themselves wholeheartedly to the service of the people and the nation.
Shri Birla observed that the Indian Police Service offers a unique opportunity to make a meaningful difference in people's lives. He urged the probationers to discharge their responsibilities with a deep sense of commitment, integrity, sensitivity and accountability, keeping public welfare at the centre of their professional conduct.
Highlighting the transformative role of technology in policing, the Lok Sabha Speaker encouraged the young officers to make optimal use of emerging technologies, digital tools, data analytics and modern investigative techniques to prevent and detect crime. He noted that technology-driven policing can enhance operational efficiency, improve responsiveness and strengthen the overall law-and-order framework.
Shri Birla further observed that the challenges facing society are constantly evolving and called upon the probationers to remain open to new ideas, continuously upgrade their professional capabilities, and adopt innovative approaches to policing. He stressed that effective policing must combine technological advancement with human sensitivity and compassion. The Speaker expressed confidence that the young officers, with their professional training, commitment and enthusiasm, would make valuable contributions towards strengthening the country's internal security and building a safe, secure and progressive India.
The interaction provided an opportunity for the IPS probationers to exchange views with the Lok Sabha Speaker and gain insights into the functioning of Parliament and India's democratic institutions.

title: PM to visit Karnataka and Gujarat on 13-14 November
subtitle:
PM to inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off various development projects worth over ₹15,600 crore in Bengaluru

Projects span key sectors including urban mobility, power transmission, renewable energy, petroleum infrastructure, waste management and railways

PM to inaugurate Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere

PM to dedicate to the nation India's largest underground LPG storage cavern in Mangaluru

PM to inaugurate four redeveloped railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme - Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road

PM to flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express

PM to participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram in Bengaluru

PM to inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium

PM to perform Darshan and Pooja at Ambaji temple in Banaskantha, Gujarat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister will visit Karnataka and Gujarat on 13-14 November. At around 10:45 AM, Prime Minister will participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. At around 12:45 PM, Prime Minister will flag off and undertake a metro ride from Tavarekere to IIM Bangalore metro station. At around 1:15 PM, Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore in Bengaluru. He will also address the gathering on the occasion
Thereafter, Prime Minister will travel to Mysuru  where, at around 3:30 PM, Prime Minister will inaugurate COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium. He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
On 14th November, at around 12 noon, Prime Minister will perform Darshan and Pooja at Ambaji temple in Banaskantha, Gujarat. Ambaji Temple is one of the 51 revered Shakti Peethas.
PM in Bengaluru
Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram, the residential headquarters campus of Swami Vivekananda Yoga Anusandhana Samsthana (S-VYASA). On this occasion, he will lay the foundation stone of the Golden Jubilee Administrative Block and launch the S-VYASA Off-Campus at Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
Being held from 13 to 23 November 2026 on the theme ‘Towards Viksit Bharat 2047’, the Golden Jubilee celebration marks five decades of institution-building and service. Established in 1975, Prashanti Kutiram was founded with the objective of integrating modern science with India's spiritual wisdom.  It is home to S-VYASA, which was declared a Deemed-to-be University in 2002 and is dedicated to education and research in Yoga.
The programme will also commemorate the birth centenary of Shri Hongasandra Venkataramaiah Sheshadri Ji, a distinguished thinker, writer and organiser born in Bengaluru in 1926. He joined the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh in 1946 and served as its Sarkaryavah from 1987 to 2000. He was among the visionaries behind S-VYASA and his inspiration and guidance played an important role in shaping the growth of Prashanti Kutiram and advancing the institution’s mission over the decades.
Prime Minister will inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off various development projects worth over ₹15,600 crore in Bengaluru. These projects span key sectors including urban mobility, power transmission, renewable energy, petroleum infrastructure, waste management and railways.
Prime Minister will inaugurate Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere, developed at a cost of around ₹3,470 crore. The new stretch will enhance urban connectivity, ease daily commuting, reduce travel time and strengthen public transport facilities in Bengaluru.
Prime Minister will also inaugurate the Transmission Scheme for Integration of Renewable Energy Zones (Phase-II) in Koppal-II and Gadag-II, developed at an investment of around ₹4,450 crore. The transmission system will facilitate the evacuation of approximately 2 GW of renewable energy potential from the Koppal and Gadag regions of Karnataka for onward transmission and distribution to beneficiaries across the grid. He will also inaugurate the Transmission Scheme for the Solar Energy Zone in Bidar, developed at an investment of around ₹1,370 crore. The project involves the establishment of a Bidar Pooling Station and will facilitate the evacuation of 2.5 GW of solar power from the region.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of the Transmission Scheme for Integration of Davanagere/Chitradurga and Ballari Renewable Energy Zones, at an investment of over ₹3,450 crore. He will also lay the foundation stone of the Transmission System Strengthening project for Integration of Additional Renewable Energy Potential at Davanagere and Ballari, at an investment of over ₹1,100 crore.
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation India's largest underground LPG storage cavern in Mangaluru, constructed at a cost of over ₹850 crore. With a storage capacity of 80,000 metric tonnes, the facility will significantly strengthen India's LPG storage infrastructure. The project also includes a 9.4 km LPG pipeline connecting New Mangalore Port to the main terminal, facilitating efficient transportation and storage of LPG. Prime Minister will also dedicate to the nation the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal of Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL), Bengaluru. Built at an investment of ₹330 crore, the state-of-the-art facility will strengthen petroleum product storage and distribution infrastructure in Karnataka.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of GAIL's Compressed Biogas Plant at Haralakunte, Bengaluru. The plant will process approximately 300 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily to produce 12.6 tonnes of clean Compressed Biogas (CBG). The project will promote scientific waste management, reduce dependence on conventional fuels and contribute to a cleaner and more sustainable environment.
Prime Minister will inaugurate four redeveloped railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme - Chamarajanagar, Chikkamagaluru, Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road. The redeveloped stations will offer improved passenger amenities and serve as city centres, promoting local commercial activities and tourism in the region.
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the 45 km Bagalkot-Wandal railway line doubling section, forming part of the 284 km Gadag-Hotgi Doubling Project. The section will improve passenger and freight movement, support local trade and facilitate coal supply to the Kudgi NTPC plant.
Prime Minister will also dedicate to the nation the electrification of the 55 km Sakleshpur-Subrahmanya Road Ghat railway section. Passing through one of India's most challenging railway terrains, the project marks a significant engineering achievement. With its completion, the entire Bengaluru-Mangaluru rail route is now fully electrified.
Prime Minister will flag off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express, providing faster and modern rail connectivity between Bengaluru, Coastal Karnataka and Goa. The service will connect key destinations including Hassan, Sakleshpur, Mangaluru, Udupi, Murdeshwar, Gokarna and Karwar before reaching Madgaon, benefiting passengers and boosting tourism in the region.
PM in Mysuru
Prime Minister will inaugurate the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, marking a significant advancement in planetarium technology and astronomy education in the country. Built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), COSMOS-Mysuru is the first LED Dome planetarium in India. Envisaged as an astronomy education and training centre, it is located on the campus of the University of Mysore at the foothills of Chamundi Hills.
The state-of-the-art facility features a 15-metre tilted dome comprising around 6,150 panels with 4.2 crore individual LEDs. Unlike conventional planetariums that use projectors to display images on a passive dome, its LED panels can be controlled in real time, offering an immersive visual experience and new possibilities for astronomy education.
The Sky Theatre will showcase professionally produced astronomy programmes, along with an in-house film exploring the connection between the history of Mysuru and astronomy. The shows will be available in Kannada, English and Hindi. The centre will also house exhibition halls, a museum featuring astronomy models and artefacts, a lecture hall, a training centre and interactive outdoor exhibits.
The centre's activities will complement the Indian Institute of Astrophysics' research, operation of multi-wavelength telescope facilities across India and in space, development of future astronomical facilities and national-level outreach programmes.

title: Cabinet approves continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units
subtitle:
Provides credit guarantee for loans extended under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana

Approval for corpus of Rs.5,000 crore facilitating PMMY loans amounting to Rs.12.6 lakh crore
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 3:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the
continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) for a period of five years upto 31.03.2031. The scheme
provides credit guarantee coverage to the Lending Institutions through National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) against default risk.
As on September 2026, more than 60.36 crore loans amounting to  Rs.43.34 lakhs crore have been sanctioned by lending institutions since launch of PM Mudra Scheme. CGFMU which was launched in January 2016 has acted as a major catalyst in enabling the growth of PMMY loans in the country.
Salient features of the Scheme:
The purpose of the fund is to provide guarantee to Lending Institutions (LIs) for the following credit facilities:
Loans extended to eligible micro enterprises under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) upto Rs.20 lakh;
Overdraft of upto Rs.10,000 provided by banks under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) accounts; and
Loans granted to Self Help Group (SHG) where portfolio is between Rs.10 lakh to Rs.20 lakh.
Guarantee coverage: Linked to the disbursement amount in case of working capital limits and outstanding amount for term loan accounts to reflect the actual risk exposure of LIs.
Guarantee Fee: Decrease in guarantee fee from @1% p.a. to @ 0.75% p.a. No change for SHG; continue to pay guarantee fee of 0.25% for the first year and 0.50% in subsequent years.
Duration of the Scheme: The Scheme would be applicable to all loans extended under PMMY during the XVIth Finance Commission Cycle i.e. FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
Impact:
Collateral free loans under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana has created a whole new generation of entrepreneurs who previously could not avail loans from formal banking system.
The extension of CGFMU scheme will enable loans of Rs.12.6 lakh crore over next 5 years
The scheme will act as a catalyst to young aspiring entrepreneurs to set up and grow their business.

title: Cabinet approves Development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block Complex, New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved the development of the
Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM)
at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi, at an estimated total project cost of
₹3,230 crore
, as appraised by the Public Investment Board (PIB).
Point-wise details
The
Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum
is envisaged as a landmark civilizational museum showcasing the continuity, diversity and richness of Bharat's civilizational heritage through an integrated narrative of its tangible and intangible cultural heritage.
The Museum will be developed through the adaptive reuse of the historic North and South Block Complex, preserving their architectural character and heritage significance while transforming them into a public cultural institution.
Spread over a proposed built-up area of approximately
1,78,509 square metres
, the Museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation. Benchmarked against major international museums, Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is going to be the museum the largest display area in the world.
The Museum will present India's civilizational journey through curated thematic galleries, exhibitions and interpretation of its diverse cultural traditions, knowledge systems, artistic practices and heritage.
The project encompasses gallery development, collection storage and conservation facilities, visitor amenities, integration of technologies and immersive experiences, landscaping, intelligent building systems and associated infrastructure.
The Museum is being developed in alignment with international best practices in museum planning, heritage conservation, exhibition design and sustainable cultural management, adapted to India's diverse cultural context.
Background
The establishment of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum was announced by the Prime Minister on 18 May 2023.
The historic North and South Block buildings, following the relocation of Government offices, provide a unique opportunity for their adaptive reuse for a significant public cultural purpose. The project seeks to preserve the architectural and heritage character of these iconic buildings while giving them a new institutional role.
The proposal was appraised by the Public Investment Board (PIB) on 27 July 2026, and the Ministry of Culture has concurred with its recommendations.
Implementation strategy and targets
The project will be implemented in a phased manner over
FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31
. The first inaugural gallery on the theme of Adornment is expected to open to public in the North Block in the later part of 2027.
A modular approach is being formulated to add more galleries. The content and collection analysis is being done and around 1.8 Million objects have been identified from National Museum and other Ministry of Culture Museums, 52 ASI site museums and various other state museums and private collections to be displayed in the YYBM.
Other galleries are being developed on the themes such as Architecture and Cityscapes, Mathematics and Astronomy, Languages and Scripts, Faith and Spirituality and Bharat Connects - Trade and Ideas, among others.
Implementation will be undertaken through coordinated project management, design and technical oversight, quality assurance and periodic monitoring.
Major impact, including employment generation potential
The Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is expected to have significant cultural, educational, economic and employment-related outcomes.
Preservation of civilizational heritage:
It will provide an integrated institutional platform for presenting India's civilizational evolution, continuity and diversity, strengthening the preservation and dissemination of tangible and intangible heritage.
Adaptive reuse of heritage buildings:
The project will give a significant public cultural purpose to the historic North and South Block buildings while retaining their architectural and heritage character.
Cultural tourism and international engagement:
The Museum is expected to emerge as a major cultural destination, attracting domestic and international visitors and strengthening India's global cultural presence and soft power.
Education and research:
It will provide opportunities for public learning, academic research, knowledge exchange and engagement with India's diverse cultural traditions and knowledge systems.
Employment generation:
The project is expected to generate direct and indirect employment during its construction and operational phases, creating opportunities for artisans, craftspeople, researchers, museologists, designers, performers and other creative professionals, besides supporting livelihoods in the hospitality and tourism sectors.
Promotion of Make in India:
Through structured vendor development initiatives, the project will encourage domestic manufacture of world-class museum materials and products, creating opportunities for Indian artisans, manufacturers, conservation professionals and technology providers.
Visitor-centric and inclusive infrastructure:
Contemporary museum technologies and accessible visitor facilities will enhance public engagement and improve the overall museum experience.
Expenditure involved
The total estimated project cost is
₹3,230 crore
, based on detailed architectural and exhibition design, engineering and museum planning requirements, including technical assessments undertaken by the concerned agencies.
The Museum is also expected to generate recurring revenue through ticket sales, food and beverage facilities, events and venue rentals, digital experiences, guided tours, retail outlets and other visitor services. The Museum is being equipped to handle a visitor flow of 1 crore visitors in a year.
No. of beneficiaries
The Museum is envisaged as a national public cultural institution, catering to the general public, students, researchers, scholars, cultural practitioners, domestic and international tourists and other visitors.
As a public cultural and educational institution, it will provide opportunities for learning, research, cultural engagement and appreciation of India's civilizational heritage. A fixed beneficiary count is not applicable to this project.
States/districts covered
The Museum will be located at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi. While the physical infrastructure is concentrated in the National Capital, the institution is envisaged to serve visitors from all States and Union Territories of India, as well as international visitors.

title: DGFT prohibits export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass to strengthen domestic recycling and critical mineral recovery
subtitle:
The measure aims to ensure domestic availability of critical minerals, strengthen battery recycling capacity and reduce import dependence

Measure to complement Government’s ₹1,500 crore Incentive Scheme for Critical Mineral Recycling
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, has prohibited the export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass falling under ITC(HS) Code 85491400. Vide Notification No. 49/2026-27 dated 10 November 2026, the export policy of the item has been amended from ‘Free’ to ‘Prohibited’ with immediate effect and until further orders. The transitional arrangements under Para 1.05 of the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP), 2023, will apply.
ITC(HS) Code 85491400 covers waste and scrap of primary cells, primary batteries and electric accumulators, as well as spent cells, batteries and accumulators, which are unsorted and do not contain lead, cadmium or mercury. The Notification specifically describes the item as Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass. Black Mass is the powdery material obtained from shredding end-of-life lithium-ion batteries and battery manufacturing waste. It contains recoverable quantities of critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese.
Critical minerals are essential inputs for electric mobility, advanced chemistry cell batteries, energy storage, electronics and renewable energy. India depends substantially on imports for several of these minerals. Recycling battery waste is among the quickest and most sustainable ways of developing a domestic supply of these resources. While the country's capacity to recycle battery waste and refine critical minerals from it has grown considerably, it is not being fully utilised due to inadequate feedstock availability. Exports of Black Mass generated in India divert this valuable secondary resource abroad, while domestic recyclers have, in some cases, had to import material to meet their requirements.
The export prohibition is intended to ensure that Black Mass generated in India is recycled and refined within the country. The measure is expected to assure feedstock availability for domestic recycling and refining units, improve their capacity utilisation and encourage further investment and employment in the sector. It will increase domestic recovery of lithium, cobalt, nickel and other critical minerals, thereby reducing import dependence and the associated foreign exchange outgo. It will also strengthen supply chains for battery manufacturing, electric vehicles, energy storage and clean-energy technologies, in line with the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Further, the measure will advance the circular economy and ‘urban mining’, reducing reliance on primary mining, while supporting environmentally sound recycling of this hazardous material within the country in accordance with applicable environmental regulations.
The measure complements the Government's initiatives under the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM), including the ₹1,500 crore Incentive Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2025 to develop recycling capacity for the separation and production of critical minerals from secondary sources such as battery waste and e-waste. Retaining Black Mass within the country will help ensure that the recycling capacity being developed under the Scheme has access to adequate domestic feedstock.
The step is also in keeping with measures adopted by several major economies to retain critical mineral-bearing battery waste and Black Mass for domestic processing.
The Notification is available on the DGFT website,
www.dgft.gov.in
.

title: Cyber Threats Respect No Borders, Neither Should Cooperation: Union MoS for Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani at ITU PP-26
subtitle:
Developing Nations Must Have a Say in Setting Global Technology Standards: Dr. Pemmasani

India's Digital Growth Must Reach Every Village says Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Showcases BharatNet at ITU PP-26
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, presented India's approach to digital connectivity, emerging technologies and cybersecurity at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) in Doha.
Speaking at the High-Level Discussion on Emerging Technologies, he highlighted India's efforts under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to make technology accessible and affordable. With 2.2 billion people across the world still offline, he pointed to India's investment of approximately $15 billion in BharatNet to extend broadband connectivity to rural areas.
He also spoke about Samriddh Gram Centres, a WSIS Prize winner, where villagers can access healthcare, agricultural advice, banking and government certificates. India's work in affordable AI computing, indigenous language AI models, quantum research and 100 5G use-case labs also featured in his address. He called for developing countries to have a greater role in framing global technology standards and spectrum policies.
On the sidelines, Dr. Pemmasani met delegations from Malaysia, Iran and Uzbekistan. Discussions covered cross-border cyber fraud, digital infrastructure security and cooperation in quantum technology.
Sharing India's experience in tackling digital fraud, he said alerts sent to banks had helped prevent suspected financial losses of over ₹5,000 crore.
"Cyber threats do not respect borders, and neither should our cooperation. Learning from each other's best practices makes all of us stronger," he said.
Began my engagements at ITU PP-26 in Doha with the High-Level Discussion on Emerging Technologies.

Under PM Shri Narendra Modi ji, India is democratising technology: affordable AI compute for our innovators, AI models in Indian languages, quantum research hubs, and 100 5G labs building talent for the future.

With a modern regulatory framework and the Bharat 6G Vision, we are preparing for a future where telecom networks, AI and satellites converge, so that connectivity reaches every remote corner.

Called for global cooperation on standards, spectrum and capacity building, so developing nations shape these technologies, not merely adopt them.

title: Government Strengthens Rural 4G Connectivity Through 4G Saturation Project
subtitle:
Number of Villages Without 4G Connectivity Declines by Nearly 75% in Four Years

BSNL’s 18000-plus 4G Saturation Sites Empowering Rural India; 1.86 Crore GB Data Consumption in October 2026

DoT Steps Up Efforts to Ensure 4G Connectivity in Unserved and Remote Villages Across India
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) is making sustained efforts to bridge the digital divide and strengthen telecommunications infrastructure across rural, remote and underserved areas of the country. These efforts have resulted in a significant reduction of nearly 75% in the number of villages without 4G connectivity, from 45,180 in 2022 to 11,372 in 2026, marking substantial progress towards expanding digital connectivity across rural India.
DoT’s 4G Saturation Project has played an important role in this expansion. The project was designed to provide 4G connectivity to 24,680 previously unconnected villages, ensuring that people in remote and underserved areas can access reliable mobile communication services and the benefits of digital connectivity. Private telecom service providers have also contributed to expanding rural 4G coverage through their network expansion initiatives.
BSNL’s 18,291 sites commissioned under the 24,680-site 4G saturation rollout plan are carrying substantial data traffic in rural areas
. In October 2026, these sites served a maximum of 10,21,048 active users in a day, who together used over 1.86 crore GB (18,659,170 GB) of data, an average of 18.3 GB per user in the month. With about 56 active users per site on average, each site is serving dispersed rural communities that were earlier outside serviceable 4G coverage.
The Government has also sanctioned an additional 26,000 mobile network sites for the next phase of expansion to address the remaining connectivity gaps. Extending connectivity to remote and geographically difficult locations remains a key challenge due to difficult terrain, high infrastructure costs, scattered settlements and the presence of remote tribal habitations. The Department is continuing its efforts to address these challenges through coordinated action with BSNL and other telecom service providers.
Way Forward
Moving forward, the Department of Telecommunications will continue to prioritise the coverage of remaining unconnected villages, particularly in remote, tribal and aspirational regions. The deployment of additional mobile network sites, expansion of network-sharing arrangements and improved utilisation of existing telecom infrastructure will remain important strategies for achieving wider rural connectivity. Greater coordination with telecom service providers and targeted interventions in geographically challenging areas will further accelerate network expansion. These efforts are aimed at ensuring inclusive digital access and enabling rural communities to benefit from digital governance, education, healthcare, financial services and other essential digital platforms.
The Department of Telecommunications remains committed to the vision of a digitally connected India, ensuring that the benefits of reliable mobile connectivity reach every corner of the country and that no village is left behind in India's digital transformation.

title: Cabinet approves Development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block Complex, New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 3:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved the development of the
Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum (YYBM)
at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi, at an estimated total project cost of
₹3,230 crore
, as appraised by the Public Investment Board (PIB).
Point-wise details
The
Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum
is envisaged as a landmark civilizational museum showcasing the continuity, diversity and richness of Bharat's civilizational heritage through an integrated narrative of its tangible and intangible cultural heritage.
The Museum will be developed through the adaptive reuse of the historic North and South Block Complex, preserving their architectural character and heritage significance while transforming them into a public cultural institution.
Spread over a proposed built-up area of approximately
1,78,509 square metres
, the Museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation. Benchmarked against major international museums, Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is going to be the museum the largest display area in the world.
The Museum will present India's civilizational journey through curated thematic galleries, exhibitions and interpretation of its diverse cultural traditions, knowledge systems, artistic practices and heritage.
The project encompasses gallery development, collection storage and conservation facilities, visitor amenities, integration of technologies and immersive experiences, landscaping, intelligent building systems and associated infrastructure.
The Museum is being developed in alignment with international best practices in museum planning, heritage conservation, exhibition design and sustainable cultural management, adapted to India's diverse cultural context.
Background
The establishment of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum was announced by the Prime Minister on 18 May 2023.
The historic North and South Block buildings, following the relocation of Government offices, provide a unique opportunity for their adaptive reuse for a significant public cultural purpose. The project seeks to preserve the architectural and heritage character of these iconic buildings while giving them a new institutional role.
The proposal was appraised by the Public Investment Board (PIB) on 27 July 2026, and the Ministry of Culture has concurred with its recommendations.
Implementation strategy and targets
The project will be implemented in a phased manner over
FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31
. The first inaugural gallery on the theme of Adornment is expected to open to public in the North Block in the later part of 2027.
A modular approach is being formulated to add more galleries. The content and collection analysis is being done and around 1.8 Million objects have been identified from National Museum and other Ministry of Culture Museums, 52 ASI site museums and various other state museums and private collections to be displayed in the YYBM.
Other galleries are being developed on the themes such as Architecture and Cityscapes, Mathematics and Astronomy, Languages and Scripts, Faith and Spirituality and Bharat Connects - Trade and Ideas, among others.
Implementation will be undertaken through coordinated project management, design and technical oversight, quality assurance and periodic monitoring.
Major impact, including employment generation potential
The Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is expected to have significant cultural, educational, economic and employment-related outcomes.
Preservation of civilizational heritage:
It will provide an integrated institutional platform for presenting India's civilizational evolution, continuity and diversity, strengthening the preservation and dissemination of tangible and intangible heritage.
Adaptive reuse of heritage buildings:
The project will give a significant public cultural purpose to the historic North and South Block buildings while retaining their architectural and heritage character.
Cultural tourism and international engagement:
The Museum is expected to emerge as a major cultural destination, attracting domestic and international visitors and strengthening India's global cultural presence and soft power.
Education and research:
It will provide opportunities for public learning, academic research, knowledge exchange and engagement with India's diverse cultural traditions and knowledge systems.
Employment generation:
The project is expected to generate direct and indirect employment during its construction and operational phases, creating opportunities for artisans, craftspeople, researchers, museologists, designers, performers and other creative professionals, besides supporting livelihoods in the hospitality and tourism sectors.
Promotion of Make in India:
Through structured vendor development initiatives, the project will encourage domestic manufacture of world-class museum materials and products, creating opportunities for Indian artisans, manufacturers, conservation professionals and technology providers.
Visitor-centric and inclusive infrastructure:
Contemporary museum technologies and accessible visitor facilities will enhance public engagement and improve the overall museum experience.
Expenditure involved
The total estimated project cost is
₹3,230 crore
, based on detailed architectural and exhibition design, engineering and museum planning requirements, including technical assessments undertaken by the concerned agencies.
The Museum is also expected to generate recurring revenue through ticket sales, food and beverage facilities, events and venue rentals, digital experiences, guided tours, retail outlets and other visitor services. The Museum is being equipped to handle a visitor flow of 1 crore visitors in a year.
No. of beneficiaries
The Museum is envisaged as a national public cultural institution, catering to the general public, students, researchers, scholars, cultural practitioners, domestic and international tourists and other visitors.
As a public cultural and educational institution, it will provide opportunities for learning, research, cultural engagement and appreciation of India's civilizational heritage. A fixed beneficiary count is not applicable to this project.
States/districts covered
The Museum will be located at the North and South Block Complex, New Delhi. While the physical infrastructure is concentrated in the National Capital, the institution is envisaged to serve visitors from all States and Union Territories of India, as well as international visitors.

The Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN)
conducted a significant operation against an interstate drug synthetic network and
busted
a clandestine laboratory manufacturing
Mephedrone (MD)
in the Tajopur Industrial Area, Mau, Uttar Pradesh under its
Operation Vajra 3.0
.
Acting on specific intelligence developed by the CBN MP Unit, a joint team of
CBN MP Unit and CBN UP Unit

11.7 kg mephedrone (MD)

Mephedrone seized at different stages of production

complete clandestine laboratory infrastructure

Dismantling of clandestine manufacturing laboratory

. Further investigation is underway to ascertain the wider interstate network, source of precursor chemicals, financial linkages and intended distribution channels.

NDPS Act, 1985

The operation reflects the continued vigilance, dedication and commitment of the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) towards combating illicit drug trafficking and clandestine manufacturing of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
CBN remains steadfast in its efforts to dismantle clandestine drug manufacturing networks, prevent the diversion of precursor chemicals, identify and disrupt interstate trafficking syndicates, enforce the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and contribute towards the national mission of a

title: India Strengthens Regional Health Partnerships as First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting Unanimously Adopts Joint Ministerial Statement in Colombo

content:
In a major step towards strengthening regional health cooperation, the First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, today unanimously adopted a Joint Ministerial Statement, reaffirming the collective commitment of member countries to advancing accessible, affordable and quality healthcare, strengthening regional health security and building resilient public health systems across the Bay of Bengal region.
Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare and Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, represented India at the historic meeting, highlighting the country's growing role in advancing regional health cooperation through knowledge-sharing, digital innovation, capacity building and collaborative action on common public health challenges.
The meeting also adopted the Revised BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030), providing a structured roadmap for cooperation in disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, digital health, traditional medicine, One Health and healthcare workforce development.
India's engagement at the meeting was further marked by significant bilateral initiatives with Sri Lanka, including the exchange of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the supply of 100 additional fully-equipped ambulances and the announcement of support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to strengthen primary healthcare services. Shri Nadda also held bilateral discussions with Nepal's Health Minister and interacted with the Indian diaspora in Colombo, reaffirming India's commitment to strengthening its longstanding partnerships in the region.
BIMSTEC Health Ministers Unanimously Adopt Joint Ministerial Statement
Addressing the inaugural meeting, Shri Nadda described the occasion as a landmark in regional cooperation, following the decision taken at the Sixth BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok in April 2025 to establish a dedicated mechanism for cooperation among Health Ministers of member countries.
He emphasised that BIMSTEC countries share both a collective responsibility and a significant opportunity to strengthen healthcare systems, improve access to quality health services and enhance preparedness against emerging health challenges.
The unanimously adopted Joint Ministerial Statement underscores the commitment of member countries to Universal Health Coverage and Sustainable Development Goal 3, while identifying key priorities for coordinated regional action.
The Statement provides a forward-looking framework for strengthening disease surveillance, emergency preparedness, early warning systems, antimicrobial resistance management, digital healthcare, traditional medicine, climate-related health responses and capacity building.
It also envisages exploring a BIMSTEC Digital Health Framework to promote telemedicine, interoperable electronic health records and the use of Artificial Intelligence in diagnostics and disease modelling.
The meeting welcomed regional initiatives, including the proposed BIMSTEC Regional Centre of Excellence for Public Health in Sri Lanka, the establishment of the BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence on Tropical Medicine in Thailand, and India's initiative to establish a Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine.
The Joint Ministerial Statement also welcomed Bangladesh's proposal for a Regional Zoonotic Disease Observatory and Early Warning System and underscored the importance of strengthening coordinated preparedness against cross-border health threats.
India Offers to Share Its Healthcare Expertise with BIMSTEC Countries
Highlighting India's progress towards Universal Health Coverage under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Nadda outlined the country's comprehensive approach to healthcare, combining expanded primary healthcare services, financial protection, modern public health infrastructure and digital innovation.
He informed the gathering that India has established over
1.85 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
, bringing comprehensive primary healthcare services closer to communities and improving access to preventive, promotive and essential healthcare.
The Minister also highlighted Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), one of the world's largest publicly funded health assurance schemes, providing annual cashless hospitalisation coverage of up to ₹5 lakh per eligible family and covering over 60 crore people.
Referring to the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), he underscored India's investments in strengthening public health infrastructure, disease surveillance, diagnostic capabilities and preparedness for future health emergencies.
Shri Nadda also highlighted the transformative role of technology in expanding healthcare access, noting that India's National Telemedicine Service,
eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore teleconsultations
.
He outlined India's experience under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in building an interoperable digital health ecosystem to improve healthcare accessibility, efficiency and continuity of care.
Reaffirming India's commitment to regional cooperation, Shri Nadda offered to share the country's experience, technical expertise and best practices with BIMSTEC Member States, particularly in primary healthcare, digital health systems and public health infrastructure.
India to Host BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at Jamnagar
In a significant initiative to deepen regional cooperation in traditional medicine, Shri Nadda announced India's commitment to hosting the
BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, Gujarat
.
The Centre is envisaged as a regional platform for collaborative research, academic exchanges, institutional partnerships, capacity building and the sharing of traditional medicine knowledge and best practices.
It will also promote evidence-informed approaches, quality and safety standards, and the responsible preservation of traditional knowledge.
The Joint Ministerial Statement welcomed India's initiative, recognising its potential to strengthen regional cooperation in traditional medicine.
India's proposal to host the next meeting of the BIMSTEC Task Force on Traditional Medicine was also welcomed.
Underscoring the importance of collective preparedness, Shri Nadda called for greater regional cooperation under the One Health approach. He highlighted that the approach aligns with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of
“One Earth, One Family, One Future”
, rooted in India's ancient philosophy of
Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam
representing India's long-held integrated approach to global health, sustainability and collaborative governance.
The Minister emphasised that that One Health is a shared responsibility and early detection, timely information-sharing and coordinated action are essential to preventing disease outbreaks and safeguarding public health.
India and Sri Lanka Deepen Healthcare Partnership; MoU Exchanged for 100 Additional Ambulances
On the sidelines of the BIMSTEC meeting, Shri J.P. Nadda held a high-level bilateral meeting with Sri Lanka's Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa, to review ongoing health initiatives and explore opportunities for further strengthening cooperation between the two countries.
In a significant outcome of the meeting, the two Ministers witnessed the exchange of an MoU for the supply of
100 additional fully-equipped ambulances
to Sri Lanka's 1990
Suwa Seriya
Emergency Ambulance Service.
The initiative will be supported through Indian grant assistance of
SLR 1,725.73 million (approximately USD 5.28 million)
and is expected to further strengthen emergency medical response capabilities, improve operational efficiency and facilitate timely access to emergency healthcare services across Sri Lanka.
India has been a longstanding development partner in the establishment and expansion of the Suwa Seriya service, having earlier extended grant assistance of USD 7.5 million in 2016 and USD 15.02 million in 2018.
These initiatives supported the deployment of 297 ambulances, which have played a vital role in providing emergency medical assistance, including during the COVID-19 pandemic and natural disasters.
The additional 100 ambulances will further build upon this successful partnership and strengthen Sri Lanka's emergency healthcare network.
India Announces Support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs in Sri Lanka
Further strengthening bilateral healthcare cooperation, Shri Nadda announced India's support for the procurement of
50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs
to enhance primary healthcare delivery in Sri Lanka.
The initiative, involving Indian grant assistance of up to
SLR 225 million
, forms part of the USD 450 million comprehensive rehabilitation package announced by the Government of India following Cyclone Ditwah, which affected Sri Lanka during November–December 2025.
The Medical Kiosks will be deployed at Sri Lanka's Arogya Primary Health Centres to provide point-of-care diagnostic services integrated with telemedicine facilities.
The initiative is expected to improve access to essential diagnostic services, enable timely medical consultations and strengthen technology-enabled primary healthcare delivery, particularly for communities requiring accessible and efficient healthcare services.
These initiatives reflect India's continued commitment to supporting Sri Lanka's health system and advancing a development partnership focused on delivering tangible benefits to people.
Shri Nadda Meets Nepal's Health Minister; Discusses Stronger Bilateral and Regional Health Cooperation
Shri Nadda also held a bilateral meeting with Nepal's Minister for Health and Food Safety, Ms. Neesha Mehta, on the sidelines of the First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting.
The two Ministers held fruitful discussions on deepening bilateral and regional health cooperation, sharing expertise and best practices, and improving access to affordable, accessible and quality healthcare.
The meeting reaffirmed the deep-rooted historical, cultural and people-to-people ties between India and Nepal, which continue to provide a strong foundation for cooperation in healthcare and development.
Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's
Neighbourhood First policy
, India reiterated its commitment to working closely with Nepal to strengthen healthcare partnerships, promote improved health outcomes and advance shared regional prosperity.
Union Health Minister Interacts with Indian Diaspora in Colombo
During his visit, Shri Nadda also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Colombo, acknowledging their invaluable contribution to strengthening the longstanding friendship and people-to-people ties between India and Sri Lanka.
Addressing the gathering, the Union Health Minister highlighted India's remarkable progress over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, particularly in healthcare, digital innovation, pharmaceuticals, medical research and technological advancement.
He emphasised that India's expanding capabilities offer significant opportunities for strengthening cooperation with Sri Lanka in healthcare, education, digital transformation and economic development.
Shri Nadda highlighted that India's
Neighbourhood First and MAHASAGAR policies
have further strengthened its enduring partnership with Sri Lanka, reflecting the shared commitment of both countries to regional stability, development and prosperity.
He appreciated the important role played by the Indian diaspora in fostering mutual understanding, enhancing cultural connections and serving as a bridge between the two nations.
A New Chapter in Regional Health Cooperation
The First BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting brought together Health Ministers and senior representatives from Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
The meeting was chaired by Sri Lanka's Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa.
The unanimously adopted Joint Ministerial Statement reaffirmed the decision to convene BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meetings and Senior Officials’ Meetings every two years, ensuring sustained engagement and follow-up on agreed regional priorities. Thailand's offer to host the Second BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting in 2028 was also welcomed.
Concluding his address, Shri Nadda expressed appreciation to the Government of Sri Lanka for hosting the historic meeting and reaffirmed India's commitment to building a healthier, safer and more resilient BIMSTEC region.
He emphasised that
“No country should be left behind in its pursuit of better health outcomes.”
The unanimous adoption of the Joint Ministerial Statement, the advancement of a common regional public health roadmap, India's commitment to hosting the Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine, and the significant bilateral healthcare initiatives with Sri Lanka and Nepal mark an important step towards strengthening regional health security and deepening India's healthcare partnerships.
Together, these engagements reinforce India's commitment to translating regional cooperation into meaningful outcomes for people, guided by the vision of inclusive development, shared prosperity and
“One Earth, One Family, One Future.”

title: NCAHP Proposes New Registration Framework to Strengthen Allied and Healthcare Professions in India
subtitle:
Draft Regulations Provide for Provisional Registration, Skill Upgradation and Transition to Regular Registration through Prescribed Competency Standards

Qualifying Examinations and Bridge Courses Proposed to Support Professional Development and Career Advancement

Integrated Digital Registration System to Enhance Transparency, Efficiency and Accountability

NCAHP Invites Stakeholder Comments on Draft Regulations by 4 December 2026
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 9:56AM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening India's allied and healthcare workforce, the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP), under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, has proposed a comprehensive regulatory framework for provisional registration of eligible allied and healthcare professionals, with clearly defined pathways for skill upgradation, competency assessment and transition to regular registration.
The proposed framework aims to bring greater uniformity, transparency and accountability to professional registration while creating structured opportunities for eligible practitioners to enhance their qualifications and competencies in accordance with prescribed standards.
To this end, NCAHP has invited public and stakeholder comments on the
Draft Provisional Registration of Allied and Healthcare Professionals Regulations, 2026
, framed under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021.
Structured Pathway for Professional Registration and Career Advancement
A key feature of the proposed Regulations is the establishment of a transparent and standardised mechanism for provisional registration of eligible allied and healthcare professionals, in accordance with the provisions of the NCAHP Act, 2021.
The framework provides for prescribed eligibility criteria, verification of credentials and clearly defined registration procedures, ensuring that professional recognition is aligned with statutory requirements and competency standards.
Importantly, the proposed Regulations also provide opportunities for eligible provisionally registered professionals to undertake
prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, supervised clinical training and minimum qualifying examinations, wherever applicable
, to meet the requirements for regular registration.
This competency-based approach seeks to promote continuous professional development, facilitate career progression and strengthen the quality of allied and healthcare services.
Strengthening Professional Standards and Quality of Healthcare
The proposed framework places emphasis on skill development, professional competence and regulatory accountability.
By linking progression to regular registration with prescribed educational and competency requirements, the Regulations seek to ensure that allied and healthcare professionals possess the necessary knowledge, skills and clinical competencies to deliver quality healthcare services.
The initiative is expected to contribute to a more skilled, organised and professionally accountable workforce while reinforcing patient safety and standards of healthcare delivery.
Digital Registration for Greater Transparency and Efficiency
The draft Regulations envisage an integrated online registration system to streamline application submission, credential verification, eligibility assessment and issuance of provisional registration certificates.
Eligible professionals granted provisional registration would receive a
Provisional Registration Unique Identification Number (PR UID)
, enabling systematic identification and regulatory oversight.
The digital mechanism aims to simplify registration procedures, improve accessibility and promote greater transparency, efficiency and uniformity across States and Union Territories.
Key Features of the Proposed Regulations
The draft Regulations provide for:
· Standardised eligibility criteria and procedures for provisional registration.
· Online application, verification and issuance of registration certificates with unique identification numbers.
· Clearly defined provisions for validity, extension, termination and appeals relating to provisional registration.
· Prescribed bridge courses for skill enhancement, competency assessments and qualifying examinations, wherever applicable.
· Supervised clinical training and institutional requirements for professional skill development.
· Transition to regular registration in the appropriate Central or State Register, subject to fulfilment of prescribed conditions.
Together, these provisions aim to establish a robust, transparent and competency-based registration system that supports professional development while maintaining healthcare standards.
NCAHP Invites Stakeholder Feedback by 4 December 2026
As part of its commitment to transparent and participatory regulation, NCAHP has invited comments, suggestions and objections from allied and healthcare professionals, professional associations, educational institutions, State Allied and Healthcare Councils, healthcare institutions, experts and the general public.
The draft Regulations are available on the official NCAHP website:
https://ncahp.abdm.gov.in/
Stakeholders may submit their feedback at
ncahp.regulations@ncahp.mohfw.gov.in
by
4 December 2026
.
The inputs received will be considered before finalisation of the Regulations.
The proposed initiative marks an important step towards establishing a
more transparent, inclusive and competency-driven regulatory ecosystem
, supporting professional growth and strengthening India's allied and healthcare workforce to meet the country's evolving healthcare needs.

title: Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, Government of India rationalizes Indian visa regime
subtitle:
Under Visa regime rationalization, main categories for Visa reduced from 13 to 09 and sub categories from 49 to 23

Indian visa regime rationalization to boost foreign tourist arrivals, enhance medical value travel and foreign student arrivals

Number of fields to be filled in the application forms for all 23 visa sub-categories reduced by 65%–70%, now application process easier, faster, and more applicant-friendly

Changes reduce overlap between visa categories and make framework easier to navigate for visitors, patients, students, researchers, investors and business professionals

Rationalization intends to boost legitimate travel, education, healthcare and economic engagement with India through clearer, purpose-based visa options
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 NOV 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah
,
the Government of India has simplified its visa regime. The step aims at making it more compact, coherent and responsive to the requirements of foreign nationals visiting India. On 27th August, 2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs reduced the number of main visa categories from 13 to 9 and the number of sub-categories from 49 to 23. This follows the earlier rationalisation undertaken in October, 2025, when the main visa categories were reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49. While considering the simplification of Indian Visa regime, the Government of India studied the Visa system of the developed countries and global standards.
The consolidation of similar purposes of travel is aimed at providing greater clarity and ease in identifying the appropriate visa category while facilitating legitimate foreign arrivals.
Currently e-visa is processed by electronic travel authorization under 13 sub categories. The facility of e-visa is presently available to the nationals of 172 countries.
Visitor Visa: greater flexibility for short and long stays
The erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed Visitor Visa, reflecting a broader range of permitted purposes beyond conventional tourism. The category has been organised into two sub-categories, V-1 and V-2, so that applicants may select a visa suited to the nature and duration of their proposed visit.
V-1 Visa
: In addition to other eligible visitor activities, it covers short-term activities such as business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats, short-duration medical treatment and short-term courses in Indian languages, music, art and craft. It is granted for 30 days with multiple entries.
V-2 Visa
: Intended for longer-duration visits, with validity of 1, 5 or 10 years, as specified. It covers the activities permissible under V-1 and mountaineering. For mountaineering, a visa of six months, with multiple entries, will be granted.
By bringing a wider range of short visits under a clearly identified category, the new arrangement makes visa selection simpler for travelers who may combine leisure with business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats or cultural learning, short duration yoga programme. The longer-duration V-2 option provides continuity and convenience for eligible repeat visitors, while the specific mountaineering provision addresses the distinct needs of such travel.
Medical Visa: continuity of care and ease of repeat visits
The Medical Visa framework retains separate provisions for treatment under conventional and AYUSH systems. M-1 Visa covers medical treatment other than treatment under AYUSH systems, while M-3 Visa covers treatment under AYUSH systems. M-1 and M-3 Visas, including their e-Visa variants, will be granted for one year as a default option with multiple entries. Corresponding medical attendant visa provisions are also available accordingly M-2 and M-4 Visas will be granted for attendant of M-1 and M-3 visa holders respectively.
This arrangement gives patients greater predictability when treatment involves multiple consultations, follow-up appointments or staged procedures. Multiple-entry validity can reduce the need for repeated visa applications during a course of care, while the distinct AYUSH provision helps applicants identify the appropriate treatment route. The availability of attendant visas also facilitates support by accompanying persons. This will encourage the Medical Value Tourism in India as per  the Prime Minister’s Vision of Heal in India.
Student Visa: clearer pathways for education and research
The Student Visa category has been consolidated into two broad sub-categories. S-1 Visa covers school, graduate and post-graduate education. S-2 Visa covers PhD and research scholars in Indian universities, visiting faculty, foreign research students visiting India for research, scientific and anthropological expeditions, internships and exchange students, among other specified academic activities.
For foreign students enrolled in Indian educational institutions through the Study in India portal, the e-S1 Visa may be granted for up to five years or for the duration of the academic course, whichever is less, with multiple entries. These provisions offer students a more readily identifiable visa pathway and greater certainty for academic planning. Longer validity linked to the course duration can also minimise procedural interruptions and make it easier for eligible students to travel during their studies.
Business Visa: clearer provisions for investment and specialized activities
The Business Visa category has been consolidated into B-1 and B-2. B-1 Visa covers long-term, licence-based business activities, including foreign nationals seeking to establish industrial or business ventures in India. B-2 Visa covers short-term, contract-based business activities, including Production Investment Business, conferences, sports, performative arts and films.
A specific provision has also been made for foreign subject-matter specialists, engineers and technical personnel engaged by Indian companies in activities such as installation and commissioning, quality checks and essential maintenance, production, IT and ERP ramp-up, training, supply-chain development, plant design and bring-up, senior management and technical support, including transfer of know-how, technology and services. Such personnel may be granted a Production Investment Business Visa under the B-2 category through the e-Visa platform. This was earlier granted under e-B4 visa nomenclature.
This differentiation gives businesses greater clarity when planning long-term investments as against short-term contractual assignments. The dedicated provision for technical specialists can facilitate timely deployment of expertise for setting up and operationalising industrial facilities, transferring technology, training personnel and supporting production, thereby improving predictability for companies and foreign professionals alike.
Simpler, purpose-based visa framework
Taken together, the changes reduce overlap between visa categories and make the framework easier to navigate for visitors, patients, students, researchers, investors and business professionals. The rationalisation is intended to support legitimate travel, education, healthcare and economic engagement with India through clearer, purpose-based visa options, subject to applicable eligibility criteria and conditions.
Simplified Visa Application Forms to facilitate Foreign Nationals visiting India
The Ministry of Home Affairs has undertaken a comprehensive exercise to simplify and rationalize visa application forms across 23 categories/sub-categories of Visas. The required filed/column for all 23 categories/sub-categories of Visas have been reduced 65%-70%. The initiative aims to significantly reduce the information required from foreign national, simplify visa form while retaining essential details necessary for visa processing. This will reduce time and effort required to complete application by the applicant as well as it will enhance administrative efficiency by facilitating more focused scrutiny and processing of visa application.
To implement all changes made in Indian Visa Regime, the MHA is updating the IT systems and by year-end, visas will be granted as per new rationalization.
The revised visa framework now comprises nine main categories as indicated below:
S. No.
Main category of visa
Purpose for which granted
1
Business Visa
Long-term business activities including establishing an industrial/business venture; short- term business activities like participation in sports & cultural/commercial performances, production investment business, attending conferences, shooting of films including documentaries & advertisement films.
2
Diplomatic Visa
Diplomats including UN Diplomats assigned to India or visiting India and their dependents
3
Work Visa
Long-term employment with Indian companies/organizations, working in NGOs and missionary activities
4
Journalist Visa
Journalists accredited in India
5
Medical Visa
Foreigners visiting India to undergo intensive/indoor medical treatment including treatment under Ayush systems and their attendants
6
Official Visa
Non-diplomatic officials including UN non-diplomatic officials assigned to India or on a visit to India and their dependents
7
Student Visa
School/graduate/post-graduate education, studies in Yoga, Vedic Culture & Indian Music/Dance, Buddhist studies, studies of Indian Languages & Indian knowledge systems, research, internship and exchange students
8
Visitor Visa
Tourism, short-term activities including business meetings, medical consultations & Wellness retreats, transit and mountaineering
9
Miscellaneous Visa
Persons of Indian Origin & their spouses/children, those coming to join various specified institutions like Auroville Foundation, dependents of foreign nationals coming on various long duration visas, stay visa for Afghanistan nationals, Long Term Visa for certain categories of nationals from neighbouring countries and other miscellaneous purposes not covered by any other visa category.
